beta-tubulin green signal remains present, diffuse cytoplasmic, no visible depolymerization, bundling, or monopolar spindles; F-actin red remains as peripheral stress fibers/cortex, no punctate collapse or loss.

candidate_mechanisms.why: Moderate support: increased cell area, cell_major_axis, nuc_area, cell_nuc_area_ratio and very high frac_large_nucleus with decreased roundness/solidity without tubulin or actin disruption is classic Aurora/polyploidy phenotype. data.note: Conclusion validated: floxuridine (PubChem CID 5790, FUDR/FdUrd) is a thymidylate synthase inhibitor (ChEMBL CHEMBL917, target CHEMBL1952) annotated as DNA replication — matching our unanimous NSC 4/4 vote and profile of large nuclei/cell enlargement with intact microtubules/actin. Mechanism causes dTTP depletion, DNA replication stress and S-phase checkpoint activation: Liu et al. on mismatch-repair-mediated checkpoint response to fluorodeoxyuridine (PMID18543256) and Washif et al. on translesion synthesis/intra-S checkpoint tolerance to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine (PMID38954736) support the observed polyploid/giant-cell phenotype vs Aurora exclusion.

reflection.text:
Unblinded as floxuridine (CID 5790) - ChEMBL CHEMBL1952 Thymidylate synthase inhibitor, name and BBBC021 structure agree (e14,e15) - which is functionally a DNA replication antimetabolite. Protocol called DNA replication 4/4 wells, correctly. What got right:

1. Quantitative profile was the driver: extreme frac_large_nucleus z=+14.6 to +17.5 and cell_area z=+9.8 to +23.5 with cell_major_axis and cell_nuc_area_ratio elevation across w_651d1c1603 3uM (e2), w_13e020007c 10uM (e3), w_1777b23edf 1uM (e6) and w_2cbb8c8990 30uM (e7). That pattern - enlarged cells/nuclei with intact density/cytoskeleton (describe_phenotype e4: density similar vs DMSO, cytoskeleton not flagged) - contradicts microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers, actin disruptors, Eg5 and protein synthesis inhibitors (as noted in hypothesis_history contradicting ids) and fits cytostatic S-phase block rather than mitotic arrest or cytotoxic loss. Cell counts 55-123 cells/well with persistence from 1-30uM supported this, not high-dose toxicity.

2. Reference comparison stabilized the call: NSC vote 2/2 then 4/4 DNA replication, k-neighbour 6/10 DNA replication (e5,e8), protocol 1-NN per well majority vote with summed similarity 1.45 (0.335-0.379 per well). This unanimity across the acquired dose range was acquired deliberately by sampling 3uM and 10uM first to find non-toxic phenotype, then 1uM for onset and 30uM for persistence (e6,e7), which was the right acquisition choice to test Aurora vs DNA replication.

3. Dose-response checks (e9 rho -0.80 p=0.2 for frac_large_nucleus, e10 rho -0.20 p=0.8 for cell_area, e11 rho -0.40 p=0.6 for frac_mitotic_like) were correctly not over-interpreted: n=4, p>0.05, no significant drop or mitotic surge, consistent with protocol note that mitotic fraction did not support Aurora. Assigning 0.72 not 0.85-0.90 was appropriate.

What misled / was ambiguous and why:

Microscopist e4 listed Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidate from 3 fields, and k-neighbour retained Aurora 2/10 then 3/10 and DNA damage 1/10 as runner-ups (e5,e8). That is understandable: polyploidy from Aurora failure can also produce large nuclei. No direct S-phase marker (BrdU/EdU, PI, pHH3, gamma-H2AX) was acquired - only morphology - so separation relied on atlas similarity and lack of mitotic enrichment. I did not miss it, but explicitly kept Aurora 0.15 and DNA damage 0.08 as alternatives in update_hypotheses (e12).

Literature found after unblinding supports the call without new experiments: floxuridine is 5-fluorodeoxyuridine, mechanism via thymidylate synthase inhibition and downstream replication checkpoint activation PMID 3155521 PMID 18543256 PMID 38954736, the latter specifically describing REV3/translesion synthesis and intra-S checkpoint activation to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine PMID 38954736 and mismatch-repair-mediated checkpoint response PMID 18543256. The unusually large nucleus/cell phenotype is consistent with drug-induced megaloblastic change described for antimetabolites PMID 6450011, which was captured here as frac_large_nucleus and cell_area elevation. No PMID in this run directly quantified high-content cell_area z-scores for DNA replication inhibitors, so that phenotypic inference is from this screen alone.

In retrospect, literature search 'DNA replication inhibitor phenotype large nuclei' returned 0 hits (e17) - did not add independent phenotype prior - but ChEMBL mechanism plus unanimous NSC vote made additional acquisitions unnecessary for this case. Next step if real lab was as stated: EdU pulse + PI for S-phase accumulation vs pHH3/gamma-H2AX to definitively separate replication stress from Aurora G2/M polyploidy.
